claimsSupported.claim: The Canal #barra archive contains university-preserved evidence of public status deflation inside the channel.
Attractiveness, vanity and social status were publicly negotiated, mocked and regulated in real time.
The channel did not only produce nickname mythmaking or status amplification; it could also publicly deflate egos and challenge self-image.
Public teasing could function as a mechanism of social regulation within the live channel audience.

analyticalReading.description: This line illustrates a counter-mechanism to nickname mythmaking and peer status amplification. A participant publicly lowers the perceived status of users who appear to overestimate their attractiveness or social value. The value of the excerpt lies in showing that the channel was an arena where ego, beauty, vanity and desirability could be challenged in public.
analyticalReading.presenceModelRelevance: The excerpt supports the IRC-Web-Presence model by showing reputation and status being negotiated live through public commentary before the channel audience.
analyticalReading.statusEconomyRelevance: The excerpt suggests that the channel had a visible status economy: participants could be elevated, mocked, desired, deflated or corrected through real-time speech acts.

limitations: The exact annex/page location still needs full indexing.
This single excerpt should not be generalized to all Canal #barra interactions.
The excerpt does not identify who the speaker was criticizing.
The excerpt does not prove a stable hierarchy of attractiveness; it supports analysis of public status negotiation and ego deflation.
